name: John of Gaunt
aliases: John of Gaunt, 1st Duke of Lancaster
role: King's uncle; Duke of Lancaster; effective head of the royal minority council
affiliation: House of Lancaster / Crown of England
description: Third surviving son of Edward III, uncle to Richard II, and the wealthiest magnate in England. Widely blamed by contemporaries for the fiscal policy -- including the 1377 poll tax -- that funded the Hundred Years' War, and for corrupt or self-interested management of the minority government. His London residence, the Savoy Palace, was deliberately and systematically destroyed by the rebels on 13 June 1381 as an act against him personally rather than general looting -- chroniclers (Knighton) record that goods were thrown into the Thames or burned rather than stolen. Gaunt himself was in Scotland negotiating a truce at the time and was not in London during the revolt; on hearing the news he placed northern castles on alert, fearing for his own safety given his unpopularity.
narrative_function: The absent target -- the revolt's clearest expression of anger at a named individual rather than an abstract grievance.
